Re: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Member: Taylor Foster
Member ID: W684120124
Reference Number: POC-157F6EFE74-80557
Date of Notice: 2026-08-23
Requested Service: Lower back disc surgery / decompression, CPT 63030
Treating Surgeon: Marchetti, MD, Orthopedic Surgery

To the Aetna Appeals Committee:

I am writing to appeal the denial of prior authorization for CPT 63030 (lumbar decompression/discectomy), as stated in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-23. The stated reason for denial was that "the requested procedure does not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity."

Aetna's own published medical policy for this category of surgery is Clinical Policy Bulletin #0743, "Spinal Surgery: Laminectomy and Fusion." That policy states that Aetna considers the following medically necessary:

"Lumbar laminectomy for individuals with a herniated disc when all of the following criteria are met: All other reasonable sources of pain and/or neurological deficit have been ruled out, including but not limited to significant pathology at other spinal level(s) on the advanced imaging radiology report that is/are not part of the surgical request resulting in incomplete surgical planning; and Member has signs or symptoms of neural compression (radiculopathy, neurogenic extremity claudication, myelopathy) associated with the levels being treated; and Advanced imaging studies (CT or MRI) indicate central/lateral recess or foraminal stenosis (graded as moderate, moderate to severe or severe; not mild or mild to moderate), or nerve root or spinal cord compression, at the level corresponding with the clinical findings; and Member has failed at least 6 weeks of conservative therapy (unless there are indications for waiver of requirements for conservative management); and Member's activities of daily living are limited by symptoms of neural compression."

The clinical record submitted with the prior authorization request demonstrates that each of these elements is satisfied:

1. Neural compression corresponding to the treated level: The MRI of the lumbar spine dated 2026-07-15 shows an L4-L5 disc extrusion with severe right lateral recess stenosis and compression of the traversing L5 nerve root. This is a single, clearly identified level of pathology consistent with the surgical request, and the exam findings (positive provocative testing on the affected side and a neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged level) confirm that the imaging finding is the source of the patient's symptoms.

2. Imaging severity requirement: The stenosis is characterized in the MRI report as "severe," which meets the policy's imaging threshold of "moderate, moderate to severe or severe; not mild or mild to moderate."

3. Signs or symptoms of neural compression at the treated level: The patient has radicular pain radiating into the right calf, consistent with L5 nerve root involvement, corroborated by positive provocative testing and a correlating neurologic deficit on examination.

4. Failed conservative therapy: The patient completed 14 weeks of supervised physical therapy (24 visits, 2026-04-03 through 2026-07-10), including core stabilization and lumbar flexibility work, as documented in the physical therapy discharge note — well in excess of the six-week conservative therapy period referenced in the policy. In addition, the patient tried four months of NSAIDs with inadequate relief and received a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-19 that produced only three weeks of partial relief. Taken together, this documents a sustained, multi-modal course of conservative management that has failed to resolve her symptoms.

5. Limitation of activities of daily living: The patient cannot stand for more than 10 minutes at a time because of pain, which is a direct and significant limitation on basic activities of daily living caused by the neural compression documented on imaging.

6. No disqualifying comorbidities: The record documents no active spinal infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and non-smoker status, so there are no other identified barriers described in the clinical summary that would contraindicate surgery.

Based on the criteria Aetna itself has published in CPB #0743, and the clinical findings summarized above, the requested procedure meets the plan's stated medical-necessity criteria for lumbar decompression/discectomy for a herniated disc with corresponding nerve root compression and failed conservative care. I respectfully request that Aetna reverse the denial and authorize CPT 63030 as requested by Dr. Marchetti.

I am enclosing the following documentation in support of this appeal:
- Physical therapy discharge note (2026-04-03 to 2026-07-10, 24 visits)
- Records of NSAID trial and corticosteroid injection (2026-05-19)
- MRI lumbar spine report dated 2026-07-15
- Office/exam notes documenting provocative testing and neurologic deficit
- [Letter of medical necessity from Dr. Marchetti, if available — not stated in the records provided]

Note on quoted material: The only plan language quoted above is text I obtained directly from Aetna's publicly posted Clinical Policy Bulletin #0743, "Spinal Surgery: Laminectomy and Fusion" (https://www.aetna.com/cpb/medical/data/700_799/0743.html). I was not able to confirm the specific version/effective date of this bulletin that Aetna applied to this member's determination, nor confirm that CPT 63030 is expressly listed in the "Applicable CPT/HCPCS/ICD-10 Codes" table of that bulletin, because that portion of the document could not be retrieved. I am relying on Aetna's own precertification guidance directing providers to CPB #0743 for lumbar decompression/laminectomy procedures. I respectfully request that Aetna confirm, in its response to this appeal, the exact version of the medical policy and criteria applied to this specific denial (reference POC-157F6EFE74-80557), including its effective/last-revised date, so that I may ensure this appeal fully addresses the criteria actually used.

Under the terms of the denial notice, this appeal is being submitted within the 180-day deadline, i.e., on or before 2027-02-19.

Please confirm receipt of this appeal and notify me and Dr. Marchetti of the outcome in writing. If any additional information is needed to complete this review, please contact me at [phone] or [email], or contact Dr. Marchetti's office at [surgeon's office phone/fax — not stated in the records provided].

Sincerely,

Taylor Foster
